title: Grateful Dead Live at Public Hall on 1973-12-06
lineage: CD > Wav > Sound Forge 9 for compression, volume and EQ  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Loud, clean soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1973 set featuring a smoking Here Comes Sunshine and an epic Dark Star jam.
ai_review.review: The remastered soundboard source is praised as louder, clearer and warm‑crunchy, delivering an excellent listening experience. Musically the show shines with a standout Here Comes Sunshine, a marathon Dark Star, a killer China Rider jam and tight Ramble On Rose, while the first set is viewed by some as less inspired. Overall fans describe it as a fun, high‑energy performance that rewards repeated listens.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of detailed reviews give five stars and praise both the performance and recording; only one low‑key review drags the average down slightly, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as louder, cleaner, crisp yet warm/crunchy; no dropout or major flaws mentioned. Reviewers note the mix is golden and the remaster improves on earlier sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set viewed by some as under‑driven and sluggish, while the second set lifts the show with tight jams and a soaring Dark Star; overall pacing moves from modest to high‑energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for distinct string bends, strong vocal delivery on Ramble On Rose, and superb interplay with Bob that lifts the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for “bringing it” alongside Keith; Phil’s bass bombs are noted as a spark in the Dark Star despite mixed opinions about overall focus.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commended for excellent interplay with Jerry, especially during melodic peaks of Here Comes Sunshine and other jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s playing is said to outshine Garcia on some tunes (Deal & Greatest Story) and adds a bluesy feel; Brent’s contributions are also called “blues‑filled”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s drumming is solid enough that listeners paused other music to enjoy this show, though no specific critiques were offered.
